newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NSW sees declining budget sector debt.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NSW sees declining budget sector debt.

text.p: The Australian state of New South Wales (NSW) said in its 1997/98 (July-June) budget that it expects budget sector net debt as a percent of gross state product (GSP) to decline to 6.2 percent by June 2000.
That is from a forecast 7.1 percent in 1997/98 and down from a high of 10.1 percent in 1993/94, budget papers released on Tuesday showed.

"The reduction in net debt since 1994 was achieved principally by using the equity restructure receipts from the electricity distribution industry and other agencies as well as the proceeds from the sale of the State Bank to repay budget sector debt," the budget papers said.
The falls over the next three years are expected before any privitisation proceeds are taken account of.
Total state net debt as a percentage of GSP is forecast at 10.6 percent in 1996/97, down from 11.1 percent in 1995/96 and 14.3 percent in 1991/92.

Superannuation is the state's largest unfunded liability, but the government is pahsing in full-funding accruing liability. This is expected to be achieved by 2020, with the unfunded liability expected to be eliminated by 2045.

The budget papers said that both Moody's and Standard and Poor's ratings agencies had recently confirmed NSW's AAA/Aaa rating for long term local currency debt and had stated the ratings outlook is stable.

"This confirmation that the state has the highest possible credit rating reflects the continuing reduction in the state's net debt, a low level of unfunded supperannuation liabilities as a percentage of GSP, the state's sound financial position and its diversified economic base," the budget papers said.
